From: Paul Smith <paul.smith@procureplus.com>

Date: 2026-08-22T13:12:00Z
Subject: ProcurePlus: Ariba enrollment + eSign exception for Order Form

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — procurement at ProcurePlus is ready to proceed with vendor enrollment into Ariba, but we have two blocking items from our legal/ops side before they will activate the supplier record:

1) They want the Order Form signed by an authorized signatory on both sides. Our platform requires a wet or DocuSign signature from the supplier side — we’ve been asked whether Redwood can accept an eSign delegation (i.e., sign by AP Director) rather than a board sign-off.
2) They asked for a completed supplier questionnaire + SOC 2 evidence link before the portal activation.

Can you confirm Redwood’s process for (1) granting an eSign exception and (2) where we should upload the questionnaire during Ariba enrollment?

I’ve copied our procurement lead (susan.li@procureplus.com) and legal (legal@procureplus.com). We’re trying to hit an end-of-month activation.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Smith
Head of Procurement — ProcurePlus
paul.smith@procureplus.com
+44 20 5555 0102

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: ProcurePlus: Ariba enrollment + eSign exception for Order Form

Paul — thanks for the clear note. We can support this, but there are a few guardrails we'll need to put in place. Proposed next steps: 

- Redwood accepts DocuSign-style eSign by delegated signatory for Order Forms only (not for the MSA). The delegation must be captured with the Signing Authority Template and evidence of authority from ProcurePlus.
- Legal will need a focused redline of the Order Form (payment, termination for convenience, data processing paragraph) — if ProcurePlus sends changes, we’ll treat them as order-form-level exceptions and not reopen the MSA.
- For Ariba: upload the completed questionnaire to the supplier onboarding attachments field; also paste a link to your SOC 2 report in the "Security Evidence" input. Ops will not activate until the questionnaire + evidence are present.

Kimberly (legal) — can you advise required language for the eSign exception and confirm a minimal evidence set? Marissa — I’ll rely on you for the Ariba attachment/process and timeline. Jonas — can you own the activation once legal signs off?

I’ll prepare an eSign exception form and a draft order-form redline and share within 24 hours.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: eSignatureException_Form.docx (requested template)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Paul Smith <paul.smith@procureplus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: ProcurePlus: Ariba enrollment + eSign exception for Order Form

Thanks — looping in legal language we can accept. Quick summary of our position and asks from ProcurePlus legal: 

- MSA: No changes required; Redwood will not reopen MSA for this engagement. Order-form-level exceptions only.
- eSign exception: We will accept DocuSign executed Order Forms if ProcurePlus provides (a) a completed Signing Authority Template, and (b) a PDF extract of the AP Director’s authorization (covering date and scope). The authorization must be within 12 months of signing.
- Required Order Form redlines (we will review but prefer these be narrow): payment terms, PO vs invoice matching, and the data processing addendum reference. Please send a redline PDF; we prefer tracked changes on a clean copy for quick review.

I’ve drafted a suggested order-form redline that keeps liability and indemnity language unchanged but tightens the acceptance criteria for POs. See attached: OrderForm_ProcurePlus_v3_redline.pdf and Signing_Authority_Template.docx.

If ProcurePlus’s legal wants to propose language that impacts liability, we’ll escalate, but I don’t expect that for typical procurement redlines.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
